interpretation: The original record consists of repair hunks. They support intent and mechanism, not a frame-exact rerender of the historical revision. The current audit compares the mutations in their frozen contemporary scenes.

A confirmed verdict can cover one component of a compound historical claim. Unreproduced and secondary-only verdicts are scoped to the documented routes, except the exhaustive two edited glyph steps. The captured 82 pairs comprise 59 primary and 23 supplemental routes.

Legacy rejection is baseline-subtracted mutation score. Only two 20 November gains required positive attribution. Seven duration-only rejections include two mutations that do paint an effect on other legal routes. A mute diagnostic is not evidence of a clear picture.

The current geometric rules use approximations. Whole-word coverage can miss a partial edge, the conservative glyph rule needs nearly complete glyph boxes, and shape/shape overlap alone cannot distinguish a docking or road from a forbidden obstruction. The existing aggregate suppresses glyph diagnoses by the traveller if any covers finding names it and keeps one longest covers run per traveller. If reporting multiple victims, deduplicate same victim/mask/time only. These limitations are possible explanations, not per-row instrumented proofs of which conditional fired.

Presence during travel means the declared subject has visible-effective ink/alpha inside its clip. Full composited legibility and the sign of a tiny grazing contact require a separate renderer-based oracle. A continuous origin/landing crossfade can be intentional.

groups.title: Route, token footprint and docking
groups.sharedCause: A centreline or endpoint was chosen independently of the ink it carries and the content occupying that space over time. Two travellers may share a route legally at different times.
groups.prevention: Reserve a lane using actual label and token extents, separate departure and docking ports, or sequence only the competing flights. Protect the part the reader needs, including non-text station rings and stops. Intentional attachment belongs to a named endpoint/phase.
groups.detection: Keep the fast ordinary covers/occluded-words checks. For narrow confirmed contact or a particular symbol, render the complete supported event and remove the named foreground and victim independently. Compare baseline, mutant and clear control. A broad-phase overlap can prune raster work. It cannot establish contact.
groups.controls: Use the complete password, poll, refusal-key and coverage-list passages. Include clear bystander, clipped/transparent/holed drawing, intended station attachment, two simultaneous disjoint travellers and a stop crossed earlier but clear at landing.
groups.implementation: Repair the four evidenced baseline clearance problems and tutorial heading now. Retain current positive detections. Reuse a native clearance assertion for preserved scene contracts. A general-purpose automatic obstacle router or ban on non-text overlap is unnecessary.

groups.title: Context lifetime and causal order
groups.sharedCause: The model computes the destination immediately. The scene must independently show which context persists, what old output clears, and which prerequisites have appeared before a later action. Fresh and rest can produce the right endpoint with a wrong middle.
groups.prevention: Keep persistent furniture separate from event-specific results. Use the existing lead/fresh/then, enter and leave at the corresponding beat. Keep each necessary prerequisite visible through its dependent trip.
groups.detection: Add one optional per-event assertion independent of the animation builder. During an exact named transient trip require exact view-scoped keyed subjects present or absent on each moving frame. A state predicate selects the applicable story. Missing/ambiguous trigger and missing required presence fail. Validate disabled/absent subjects from a witnessed endpoint or explicit resolvable subject so a typo cannot pass. Distinguish effective alpha/clip presence from full composited readability.
groups.controls: Check browser rack-before-handout, sessions wax-before-ticket, persistent conversation ledger, and old exhibit or door during the next Poppy trip. Poison order, source survival, broad fresh and missing anchor separately. Permit intentionally withheld answers and a still-visible reference.
groups.implementation: Implement a small runtime/check integration for both authored replay and reachable reader events. Carry the event boundary through grouped replay, seek and repeated trips. Leave purely editorial intent with the author who can express a concrete assertion.

groups.title: Unique objects and copied information
groups.sharedCause: A travelling proxy, its source and its destination use different drawing keys. Generic pass and flight do not know that a live source in a different slot represents the same physical object. Conversely reading a code legitimately copies it.
groups.prevention: Construct one carry operation that retires the named source as its proxy appears, optionally substitutes a different target drawing on arrival, and lets the caller restore a borrowed source at a later beat. Continue using pass for messages and explicit copies.
groups.detection: Apply the same phase assertion to the source during the named travel. Use a required target during the subsequent action for causal handoff. Judge the moving interval after departure so a co-located two-image crossfade is legal.
groups.controls: A separated wordless solid ring must reject. An outline marking the empty slot, a genuine duplicate value at a separate port and a source-to-target crossfade at one port must pass. Test repeated events, reverse travel and later skill-card restoration.
groups.implementation: Use the existing c.travel/leave/enter operations and existing durations. One source of timing avoids separate source leave and mover appear calls drifting. Do not mark every repeated label or equal-shaped item as a duplicate.

groups.title: Identity, rearrangement and text replacement
groups.sharedCause: The same model identity can keep its key while its screen composition or displayed content changes. Interpolating each matching leaf independently can transport labels, mix incompatible page shapes, or open a temporary gap inside one address.
groups.prevention: Decide whether a part carries narrative travel, remains continuous context or is replaced at rest. Keep a compound URL and an incompatible page layout atomic. Distinct layout keys and whole-word matching already support replacement.
groups.detection: Where authors have chosen stationary labels, check that their actual readable positions are confined to old/new arrangement or check an invariant relationship between labelled components. Use phase assertions for persistent context. No geometry-only decision can determine whether an unobstructed slide helps the explanation.
groups.controls: Preserve meaningful travel of a person taking a new seat and deliberate camera or layout motion. Separately test an applicable same-key changed word with whole-text and by-place choices. The historical 1,564 identical glyph frames cannot validate those choices.
groups.implementation: Keep existing correct reflows. Put narrow endpoint/compound-layout assertions in the owning scene tests for commitments that matter. Do not introduce a catalog-wide displacement threshold.

groups.title: Beat accounting and editorial pace
groups.sharedCause: Adding serial beats, lengthening fades or stretching the event envelope changed elapsed time independently of the intended teaching sequence. A too-small allowance is mechanical. An acceptable but slow valid sequence needs an author’s timing or narrative criterion.
groups.prevention: Budget all actual serial and parallel beats for each branch. Collapse redundant legs or shorten a beat only if the explanation remains clear. Preserve the existing refusal to compress an overlong score.
groups.detection: Machine already compares authored duration with allowed runtime on the normal send path. Keep guard-only as a separate outcome. For a specifically agreed time budget or maximum number of legs, test that event using the real clock. The five-second ceiling is a coarse independent regression.
groups.controls: Guard the three historical squeezed edits. Accept a legal fast first direct ask and a complex slow route. For coverage report, assert the two named explanatory legs if that editorial decision is pinned.
groups.implementation: No tighter universal time cap. Keep rejection reporting separate from material that actually painted. Add branch-specific time or beat assertions only where an author has established the requirement.

groups.title: Legibility of the travel representation
groups.sharedCause: A scaled full-detail resting card keeps its printed literal while losing the size needed to read it during motion.
groups.prevention: Choose a readable travel-sized code when its actual value is meaningful, or carry a wordless symbol and show the literal at rest.
groups.detection: Retain the existing small-words check against whole-picture phone reading size and the scene’s resting words. Confirm scale and real glyph contribution in phone captures.
groups.controls: Reject all three audited tiny-literal examples. Accept a wordless compact token and a readable full-size travelling literal. A large rendering enlarged after capture is an inadequate phone control.
groups.implementation: Existing prevention and checker are adequate for these three reconstructions. The independent glyph pairing/provenance problems belong to text identity and inspection.

implementationPlan.title: Repair observed baseline contact
implementationPlan.change: Move the direct password card outside the page until the field approach, route the pending device poll clear of the full company name including its final approach, inspect and clear the refusal-key lanes on both returns, and remove coverage-list grazing on the desk heading. Use the complete render interval. Treat the slight sessions stamp contact near docking as a separate named attachment judgment.
implementationPlan.verification: Assert moving and victim-only ink before counting restored pixels. Use full, without victim, without mask and without both under the same renderer, time and clip. Use independently chosen bystanders and a positive poison. Record the earliest and worst confirmed contacts and the relevant event. Do not accept an all-zero comparison with missing subjects.

implementationPlan.title: Check a small number of declared relationships
implementationPlan.change: Use one state-conditioned event contract with exact transient trigger and present/absent subjects. Keep it independent of the helper constructing the transition. Pilot the rack row before page handout, on-wax key before ticket, persistent ledger during a turn and stale exhibit during a new request. Use the same relationship for the unique source during a transfer.
implementationPlan.verification: Validate each relationship on public playback and reachable machine sends. Fail unusable triggers, typoed or ambiguous selectors and an absent prerequisite. Exercise reversal, re-entry, repeat, grouped replay, seek, expected old-result disappearance and coincident source/target overlap during fade.

implementationPlan.title: Make ownership transfer explicit
implementationPlan.change: Add a small helper over travel/leave/enter for a named source and proxy, with an optional destination handoff. Retain existing public flight/pass behavior. Match the gesture’s source representation or explicitly supplied token. Leave later restoration under the caller’s control.
implementationPlan.verification: A published key cannot stay solid on the chain during travel, a password plate may turn into field dots on arrival and a borrowed skill card may return on a later ticket beat. Reading a copied code must preserve its source.

implementationPlan.title: Preserve logical text ownership in matching
implementationPlan.change: In src/animation.ts, pairParts adds bare target frames under frameOfT’s nearest mapped frame. Point-free keyed groups such as owner:card are skipped, although the copied text itself retains its own metadata. Carry the bypassed target ancestry as internal diagnostic provenance through actual interim admission. Sampling must respect the real paint order, clips and actual glyph geometry.
implementationPlan.verification: Reverse target admission in an isolated outside-corpus poison. Require the intended owner, words, covering shape and interval in the middle of the animation, with the normal order clean. Check nested and repeated text under different owners, a partly keyed ancestor, masked-by-clip controls and seeking. Avoid changing render geometry, public matching keys or frame endpoints for diagnostic convenience.

implementationPlan.title: Keep the historical inventory and attribution reviewable
implementationPlan.change: Separate comparable raw rejection from observed historical defect, secondary effect, guard refusal and stale or editorial entries. Keep original IDs, mutation semantics and audit footage tied to the frozen commit. New drift fixtures and synthetic harms receive distinct IDs. A protected path through a changed scene may need a mechanical context rebase of the edit while preserving the original mutant behavior.
implementationPlan.verification: Run all 59 baseline-subtracted mutations, the eight every-event Poppy baselines and the rest of the catalog. Check exact expected findings on the scenario, event, part, victim or required prerequisite. Preserve historic visual verdicts even where newer source changes the differential. Show any revised measurements separately.

implementationPlan.title: Close the integration failures
implementationPlan.change: Move sorted:name outside the sweep of the incoming sorted boxes in the canonical sort-as-text picture and the literal docs/WRITING.md tutorial source. Point packaged docs/MOTION-CORPUS.md to the repository evidence URL because the evidence directory is absent in the installed package.
implementationPlan.verification: Exercise both tutorial caption and done stages, package-link test and packed package. Run typecheck, repository suite and catalog gates. Scene tests use public imports, fidelity.ts may use its existing internal test helpers. Keep the frozen round-3 benchmarks unchanged.

cases.historicalClaim: A full-size ticket rode each lane over the lane’s name, which sat on the line on a plate; the fix set names above the lines and sent a token at 0.28 scale under them.
cases.historicalCause: The lane’s name occupied the road and the author reused the complete resting ticket as the traveller.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Removing nameAt above and enlarging the token puts the opaque paper over API at f30. The adapted LEAD includes its plate.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause
cases.rawDiagnostic: legacy fresh finding without mandatory attribution

archivedSample.line: step "seal", play 1, event 1: covers: part “ticket:flight” at 0.933 s travels over “API” (part “lane:api:name”), covering 100% of it, for 0.33 s before it lands; fix: route it round the label (or under it, scaled down), or move the label off its way

cases.recommendation: The existing covers rule names this ticket and API. Keep names clear of the swept ticket and use a wordless travel size. Test the name while the token passes, including the approach and handoff.

cases.historicalClaim: The key flew to the agent, and back at sign-out, at full size over the station’s name and the lane names; the fix flies it at half size.
cases.historicalCause: Both legs used the resting key at full size. The centreline allowed its teeth and ring to intrude into neighbouring names.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Removing the two half-scale operations cuts Sign-in lettering on the outward and return trips. The station name is clear in both recorded routes.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause
cases.clauseVerified: The incoming and returning keys cut lane lettering. Neither recording covers the station name.
cases.supplementalFindings: On the returning key, the lane-name knockout recovers 50 pixels at f23. The station name remains clear.
cases.recommendation: The existing detector misses the visible lane contact. Verify lane ink on both trips. Do not attribute contact with the station name or judge the key by a filled bounding box.

cases.historicalClaim: The last event’s exhibit and closed door stayed while the next ticket travelled, and changed only when it had landed; the fix lists them in beats’ fresh, so they go before it sets off.
cases.historicalCause: Event-scoped drawings were treated as persistent scene context. The default rest carried the old exhibit or closed door past the start of the next event.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Dropping exhibit and door from FRESH retains the wax object through the request and retains the barrier/message through the document flight. The original exhibit words do clear on the first route.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause
cases.supplementalFindings: During Discover the closed barrier and “no way in yet” also stay while the document travels. They retain painted ink through f78 in the variant and only through f6 in the baseline.
cases.recommendation: Baseline already clears them. During the appropriate named trip assert the old exhibit or door is absent. A surviving reference station exercises the opposite expectation.

cases.historicalClaim: A request’s ticket set off from the agent’s seal and crossed the station on its way to the lane; the fix launches it on its lane, clear of the station.
cases.historicalCause: A seal-centred launch sent a full ticket through the station before it reached the lane.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Reinstating seal-to-lane points visibly covers the station ring on expire. Changing sendAgain also lengthens a later answer beyond its allowance.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause

archivedSample.line: duration guard: machine.send("answer"): authored transition lasts 3.450 s but the event allows 3.400 s; increase the machine runTime or shorten the transition instead of compressing its fades

cases.recommendation: Existing raw rejection is a duration guard on another route. Assert the station ring stays visible during launch on expire. Preserve the separate answer refusal.

cases.historicalClaim: The ticket was launched just clear of the station, so it set off over the lane’s name; the fix launches it past the name.
cases.historicalCause: The launch calculation allowed for station and ticket widths but omitted the space occupied by the lane name.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Moving launchAt back to the station edge masks API as soon as the ticket appears.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause
cases.rawDiagnostic: legacy fresh finding without mandatory attribution

archivedSample.line: step "turned-back", play 2, event 1: covers: part “ticket:flight” at 0.500 s travels over “API” (part “lane:api:name”), covering 123% of it, for 0.60 s before it lands; fix: route it round the label (or under it, scaled down), or move the label off its way

cases.recommendation: Existing covers can name API. Keep the departure port beyond the painted name and half the ticket width. Exercise the widest supported lane label and ticket.

cases.historicalClaim: When the MCP lane came or went, the API lane slid to its new height: motion for the layout; the fix keys the lanes apart in the two layouts and cross-fades them.
cases.historicalCause: One identity was reused for two layout variants. Morphing a shared key interpreted the API row’s new height as travel.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Reusing the ids makes the label and rule move together by 46 screen pixels. A static crossfade also conveys the change in lane count.
cases.disposition: authored interpretation required
cases.recommendation: Baseline already chooses separate layout identities. If this editorial decision must hold, assert the visible label is at the old or new row, while the ticket remains free to move.

cases.historicalClaim: The first fix for the sliding lanes listed them in beats’ fresh: they faded out and came back only after the ticket had travelled, so it flew on no lane; the second cross-faded them before it set off.
cases.historicalCause: The early fix treated the supporting roads as stale results. Their replacements were deferred until after the traveller that needed them.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Selecting fresh lane prefixes and omitting relay leaves the ticket crossing an empty stage on MCP.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause
cases.recommendation: Flicker’s flight exemption cannot express this dependency. Require the current lane’s named stroke during the ticket trip on relayout, using mcp-api/mcp-mcp as appropriate to the event.

cases.historicalClaim: A new delegation (or seal) came up from under the station, across its name, to the seal; the fix brings it from off the stage above.
cases.historicalCause: The author chose an entrance below the station for a seal-bound emblem, directly through the station name.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Restoring the lower first waypoint sends the filled emblem through your agent at f24.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause
cases.rawDiagnostic: legacy fresh finding without mandatory attribution

archivedSample.line: step "seal", play 1, event 2: covers: part “delegation” at 0.800 s travels over “your agent” (part “agent:name”), covering 42% of it, for 0.20 s before it lands; fix: route it round the label (or under it, scaled down), or move the label off its way

cases.recommendation: Existing covers names the emblem and words. Keep the upper approach and verify the label through the transition. The emblem can attach to the seal at its end.

cases.historicalClaim: The MCP key came down 1.2 units right of its hook, over the words “for MCP”; the fix brings it down 2.6 units right, past them.
cases.historicalCause: The descending MCP key used a lane close to its hook caption. The historical repair shifted the descent farther right.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Moving the descent inward cuts MCP and your agent. The for MCP caption first has sampled ink at f92, well after the flight. The audited baseline also grazes a lane name.
cases.disposition: only a different effect was demonstrated
cases.supplementalFindings: The hook caption first has sampled ink at f92 in both versions, long after this key flight.
cases.recommendation: Protect the actual lane and station lettering on both routes and repair residual baseline contact. Test a hook caption only in a state where it paints. Record this historical target as secondary-only.

cases.historicalClaim: A refreshed key came back along the lane over the lane’s name; the fix routes it under the name.
cases.historicalCause: A large key returned along a road that also contained the API label. Only the later fix offset the return lane.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Restoring the direct points puts the key over API at f38. The lower baseline route still grazes a smaller part of a lane name earlier.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause
cases.recommendation: The historical mutation has no fresh diagnostic here. Give the key’s painted ring and teeth clearance along the entire return. Check the real label with an object-removal control.

cases.historicalClaim: The agent’s ticket came in diagonally from under the stamp, across it; the fix brings it in level from the stamp’s side.
cases.historicalCause: A diagonal from the stamp side placed an arriving sheet across the stamp, obscuring their relationship before docking.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Restoring the raised, offset origin covers the lower stamp at f15. The baseline level approach has minor later contact at the destination.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause
cases.rawDiagnostic: legacy fresh finding without mandatory attribution

archivedSample.line: step "send", play 1, event 1: covers: part “ticket:flight” at 0.467 s travels over “until 06:00” (part “chain:until”), covering 60% of it, for 0.30 s before it lands; fix: route it round the label (or under it, scaled down), or move the label off its way

cases.recommendation: The archived covers sample names until 06:00. Specify the stamp as a protected graphic during approach and inspect the designed docking contact separately.

cases.historicalClaim: When the published key pressed the seal, nothing showed it moving: it left the chain and appeared on the wax only as the picture settled, after the punches it caused; the fix sends it down first.
cases.historicalCause: The model reached the validation state at event start, but the view postponed the visible cause until rest. Entering the final pose alone lost the travel that explained the check.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Removing hand and the chain lead leaves the key hanging while the ticket moves and validation starts. The link has ink at f82 and the on-wax key only at sampled f99. The baseline key is already there at f36.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause
cases.supplementalFindings: The validation link is visible by f82 in the variant, before the on-wax key at sampled f99. In the baseline that key is already visible at f36 and the link appears by f94.
cases.recommendation: Require the named on-wax representation during the ticket’s trip on the branch that uses it. Assert a source-to-wax transfer separately so teleporting a key early cannot satisfy the full claim.

cases.historicalClaim: The published key flew to the wax while it still hung in the chain, so it was in two places; the fix takes it out of the chain as the trip begins.
cases.historicalCause: The traveller represented an existing key, yet transferring its ownership required a separate source leave.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Dropping the chain-ring leave from the takeoff group draws a solid ring on the chain during the visible ring flight. The empty slot in the baseline is a different drawing.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause
cases.recommendation: Use a carry operation and an independent absence check on the solid ring during travel. Permit an empty outline and coincident takeoff crossfade. Text-duplication rules cannot see these separated rings.

cases.historicalClaim: Every tamper ran in a fixed 2.6 s runTime, while its beats lasted 3.1 s (4.35 s with the published key’s trip), so they were squeezed into it; the fix gives each transition its own length. Undone with the beats as they were then.
cases.historicalCause: One fixed event allowance covered branches with different authored beat sums. Earlier playback fitted both sequences into that allowance.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: The adapted reconstruction restores 2.60 s and longer beat components. Today 3.060 s on send is refused before paint.
cases.disposition: prevented by event guard on claimed overrun

archivedSample.line: duration guard: machine.send("send"): authored transition lasts 3.060 s but the event allows 2.600 s; increase the machine runTime or shorten the transition instead of compressing its fades

cases.recommendation: Retain the strict duration guard and cover both key-journey branches. Report guard prevention. Testing a hypothetical compressed movie would require a separate historical engine experiment.

cases.historicalClaim: A tamper took 3.1 s, and 4.35 s with the published key’s trip; the last audit commit shortened every beat.
cases.historicalCause: Successive entrances, travel, stamp, punches and settle each received time. The accumulated delay prompted an editorial retiming.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Restoring the longer component times and event allowance yields 4.35 s versus 3.90 s for the published-key route, still in the same causal order.
cases.disposition: authored interpretation required
cases.supplementalFindings: The ticket first has sampled travel ink at f51 in the baseline and f60 in the variant.
cases.recommendation: Both satisfy the duration guard. If the author adopts a maximum for this particular sequence, check it at the event boundary and retain a slower legitimate complex event as a control.

cases.historicalClaim: When the page opened, you and the agent slid to your places beside it, motion that says nothing about the protocol; the fix cross-fades them.
cases.historicalCause: Persistent person and station keys were interpolated across compositions even though the narrative event was the request.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Suppressing the relaid list visibly transports the people. A tag masks Exchange items during that move. Frames establish the obstruction while the educational value of the slide remains editorial.
cases.disposition: only a different effect was demonstrated

archivedSample.line: step "reask", play 1, event 1: occluded words: part “page:hint” at 3.433 s “password” stays readable by opacity but “agent:station”, an opaque foreground shape, covers at least 90% of 3 glyph boxes for 0.10 s; fix: draw the words above their paper, route the foreground shape round them, or take the old words away before covering them

cases.recommendation: The existing attributed finding is secondary occluded words. Keep the authored reflow treatment and validate this exact tag/line pair plus a purposeful unobstructed move.

cases.historicalClaim: When the page closed after the code came back, you and the agent slid back across the stage; the fix cross-fades them.
cases.historicalCause: The page closes to a new composition. Unhandled shared participant keys are morphed during final rest.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Emptying the moved list leaves the old layout in place, then slides the station up and the person down. The baseline replaces them at their new positions.
cases.disposition: authored interpretation required
cases.recommendation: Preserve the layout intent with an endpoint-only placement assertion on these people if required. The code, key and tag genuinely travel and must still do so.

cases.historicalClaim: A code coming back with tokens took 4.8 s; the fix brought it to 3.3 s.
cases.historicalCause: The authored event envelope stretched the whole return of the code, key and tag. The historical 3.30 s cut applied to an earlier choreography.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Changing the current allowance to 4.80 s stretches a legal 4.45 s sequence. The present differential is 0.35 s, and the order stays intact.
cases.disposition: authored interpretation required
cases.supplementalFindings: The baseline tag flight has sampled ink at f81–108 versus f87–117 in the variant.
cases.recommendation: An agreed event-specific maximum can be checked mechanically. Do not promote the obsolete 3.30 s historical value to a requirement. Retain the actual transition times.

cases.historicalClaim: The request and the poll went straight from the seal to the desk or the address bar, full size, over the labels of the agent’s side; the fix routes small tokens along the gap between the strip and the keyring.
cases.historicalCause: Full-size request paper and direct routes consumed space intended for the agent’s labels. Multiple edits affect two motions and both flows.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Undoing token scale and the approach routes overlaps the key/password artwork on the recorded direct re-ask. No agent-side word loss was demonstrated there. On the device poll, 369 company-name pixels are hidden at f31 versus 104 in the baseline.
cases.disposition: only a different effect was demonstrated
cases.supplementalFindings: Separate direct/device first asks and the pending device poll were replayed. At poll f31 the larger slip hides 369 company-name pixels versus 104 in the baseline.
cases.rawDiagnostic: legacy fresh finding without mandatory attribution

archivedSample.line: after ask, approve-read, collect, ask, collect: covers: part “poll” at 0.767 s travels over “refresh token” (part “tag”), covering 42% of it, for 0.20 s before it lands; fix: route it round the label (or under it, scaled down), or move the label off its way

cases.recommendation: The old raw covers sample is on another history and label. Keep the narrow travel form and test named agent-side targets only where they paint. Repair and retest the established device-card baseline contact.

cases.historicalClaim: The password in the page was not listed in beats’ fresh, so on a second approval it stayed in the field while your card was still on its way to it; the fix lists it.
cases.historicalCause: A previous password value could historically remain in the field while the next password was still being delivered.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Removing page:password from FRESH no longer produces that source state. Immediate reapproval is refused. Reasking clears approval and both legal second approvals have identical SVGs and pixels across 72 frames apiece.
cases.disposition: unchanged on the audited routes
cases.supplementalFindings: Both legal second-approval routes have matching original SVG and pixel sequences.
cases.recommendation: Keep the historical no-op. In a separate feasible fixture with an already filled field assert the old value clears during the next authenticated handoff. Do not change model legality to manufacture a corpus gain.

cases.historicalClaim: The request’s token appeared and left in 0.15 s, inside a 2.2 s runTime its beats overran, so they popped; the fix gives them 0.25 s and the event 2.6 s.
cases.historicalCause: Short fades and a single small allowance were combined across distinct request branches whose beat sums differed.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: The first direct request paints with 0.15 s fades. The reconstructed direct re-ask requires 2.80 s and first device request 3.90 s against 2.20 s, so their overrun never paints.
cases.disposition: prevented by event guard on claimed overrun
cases.supplementalFindings: The first direct request is visible at sampled f9–42 in the variant and f15–81 in the baseline. Both rejected routes have a saved paired receipt and a guard proof.

archivedSample.line: duration guard: machine.send("ask"): authored transition lasts 2.800 s but the event allows 2.200 s; increase the machine runTime or shorten the transition instead of compressing its fades

cases.recommendation: Guard prevention applies to the overrun. Keep both failing routes and the legal faster direct request. An independently specified minimum readable exposure would be needed to call that first entrance too fast.

cases.historicalClaim: A page of another shape (the website before the phone) was still there while the new one faded in over it; the fix takes the old page away first.
cases.historicalCause: Keys shared across a website and phone frame were left alive while the replacement composition entered.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Removing reopen and retaining to-side stale keys holds the old website/field beneath the moving person and morphs a single outline into the phone. The recorded route does not show two concurrent outlines.
cases.disposition: only a different effect was demonstrated
cases.recommendation: Declare the old composition cleared before the device stage, or use distinct variant identities and explicit replacement. Verify the old frame’s footprint during the switch. Do not count a double-outline detection.

cases.historicalClaim: The device card came from the Company’s desk, where it does not come from; the fix brings it from the agent’s seal.
cases.historicalCause: The origin was chosen for compositional convenience. The author meant the code shown by the agent to depart the seal.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Reverting the origin shows the visual card travelling from the Company desk. The model and caption distinguish issuing credentials from the agent presenting them.
cases.disposition: authored interpretation required
cases.recommendation: Agree which act the motion represents. Test the first drawn card against that actor’s authored port for this event, with a genuine desk-issued object as a positive counterpart. Geometry cannot select the actor.

cases.disposition: prevented by event guard on claimed overrun

archivedSample.line: duration guard: machine.send("check"): authored transition lasts 1.850 s but the event allows 1.550 s; increase the machine runTime or shorten the transition instead of compressing its fades

cases.recommendation: Retain the guard. To validate the ordering contract on paint, test a separate legal-duration fixture with old register ink while the issuer arm is drawn.

cases.historicalClaim: The fetched sheet dropped from the address bar straight down over the shop’s fascia to the doorstep, while the address was still changing; the fix changes the address first and brings a document down the street beside the shop.
cases.historicalCause: The old fetch combined an address change with direct document descent through the shop. These are two independent route and timing decisions.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: The adaptation changes only the waypoints. It cuts the lower doorway, is outside the building at fascia height, and leaves after the address settles. No shop-name loss on any of seven offered choices. Upload uses the board.
cases.disposition: only a different effect was demonstrated
cases.supplementalFindings: All seven offered server choices were replayed. No shop-name glyph is covered in any. The upload route uses the noticeboard in both versions.
cases.recommendation: The doorway contact is secondary. Keep the street itinerary and address-first sequence. Name the protected object and window separately if writing route or ordering assertions.

cases.historicalClaim: The fetch’s document appeared and left in 0.15 s and the barrier had a beat of its own, in a 1.3 s runTime the beats overran; the fix gives the token 0.25 s, folds the barrier into the settle and the event 1.5 s.
cases.historicalCause: A short fixed budget had to accommodate fetch fades, movement, a separate barrier beat and settle.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: The adaptation restores short fades and a distinct barrier. At 1.750 s versus 1.300 s the first fetch is refused before paint.
cases.disposition: prevented by event guard on claimed overrun

archivedSample.line: duration guard: machine.send("check"): authored transition lasts 1.750 s but the event allows 1.300 s; increase the machine runTime or shorten the transition instead of compressing its fades

cases.recommendation: Retain the strict guard and a legal concurrent barrier/settle control. No observed compressed fade can be attributed to the current engine.

cases.historicalClaim: When a redirect shortened the host, the URL’s path slid left; the fix replaces the whole URL.
cases.historicalCause: An address was split into independent keyed host and path pieces. On redirect only the changed host was replaced, so the unchanged path continued to occupy the old offset.
cases.currentMechanismAndLimits: Removing the explicit whole-URL replacement shows a shortened host alongside a misplaced path that then slides left from x310 to x242.
cases.disposition: baseline improved on the demonstrated clause
cases.recommendation: Replace this compound text atomically. An independent check can require that whenever both components paint, their relative join matches the old or new address arrangement. Ordinary movement of a complete address remains valid.
